A game for learning. Not trading advice. Scores are saved only in this browser.

What it does

“Make me a market” is the classic trading-interview exercise: quote a price you would buy at and a price you would sell at on something uncertain, let others trade against you, learn something, and adjust. This turns it into a four-level arcade game with an 8-bit look.

How it works

  1. Each market has a hidden value: the sum of three dice (3–18) at level 1, or the sum of cards drawn from a deck of 1–10 (four of each) at later levels.
  2. You quote a bid and an ask no wider than the level's maximum spread. Bots trade one unit each against your quote: they buy at your ask or sell at your bid.
  3. One item is revealed, and you quote again. When everything is revealed the market settles: P&L = cash + inventory × true value.
  4. Level 3 adds a news event about the last card, which shifts the distribution. Level 4 adds a position limit and a tighter spread.

Teaching mode shows the expected value and range after each reveal, how your quote compared, and at the end splits your P&L into spread capture (what you earned by quoting around the expected value) and adverse selection (how much the truth moved against the positions you were handed). The bots' rules are on How the bots think.

Why I built it

Limits

  • Bots trade one unit at a time and never quote back; there is no order book.
  • The card distribution treats the remaining deck as if drawn with replacement, which is a close approximation for a 40-card deck.
  • Scores live in this browser only. Clearing site data clears them.
